content.title: Team USA beats Canada to advance to WBC semifinals against Dominican Republic: Live updates and reaction
content.text: Follow our live coverage as USA makes the final four in Winter Baseball ClassicMason Miller closed out Team USA’s WBC quarterfinal win over Canada at Daikin Park. Getty ImagesUSA beats Canada — ReactionTeam USA has beaten Canada 5-3 in the WBC quarterfinals to set up a star-powered clash with the Dominican Republic in the semifinal round.Logan Webb threw 4.2 scoreless innings for Team USA. The U.S. got a run-scoring groundout from Kyle Schwarber in the first inning, an RBI single by Alex Bregman with another run scoring on an error in the third, and RBI singles from Brice Turang and Pete Crow-Armstrong in the sixth. The Americans’ bats then went cold against Canada’s relievers, as Canada struck back with a three-run sixth highlighted by a Bo Naylor 2-run home run. But David Bednar escaped a two-on, no-out jam in the seventh and Mason Miller slammed the door by striking out the side in the ninth to send the U.S. to Miami, where it will face a Dominican Republic team every bit as loaded with MLB superstars as the Americans.Share your thoughts: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMore drama tomorrow! Getty ImagesWe’ll have more excitement for you tomorrow as well as the other two World Baseball Classic quarterfinals get underway.First, Italy takes on Puerto Rico in a matchup of two of the biggest surprises in this WBC. The Italians seek their first-ever trip to the semifinals while Puerto Rico looks to get back there after getting upset by Mexico in this round three years ago.Then, Shohei Ohtani’s Japan team takes on a Venezuela squad full of notable MLB talent in its own right, headlined by 2023 National League MVP Ronald Acuña Jr.We’ll have both games covered live right here on The Athletic!An offense that’s firing Getty ImagesWondering how impressive Dominican Republic’s offense has been at this World Baseball Classic? Well there’s a taste of it below …1: Dominican Republic — 51 runs, 49 hits, 50 RBIs, .312 batting average2: United States — 40, 49, 36, .2833: Japan — 34, 37, 33, .3014: Italy — 32, 40, 28, .294Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has delivered in his first World Baseball Classic — the Toronto Blue Jays star is 7-for-14 with two doubles, two home runs and eight RBI.Oneil Cruz has also maximized his opportunities off the bench with four runs, three hits (including two home runs) and three walks in seven plate appearances — he now could get a chance to hit against Pittsburgh Pirates teammate Paul Skenes on Sunday.Tasty.Familiar faces for Judge Getty ImagesAaron Judge plays his MLB home games in the Bronx, home of one of the most famously Dominican-heavy enclaves not only in New York City but in the U.S. as a whole.But that might not be the only source of familiarity when he takes the field in front of what’s expected to be another Dominican Republic-favoring crowd in Miami on Sunday, as has been the case for all D.R. games at Miami’s loanDepot Park to this point.Luis Severino, the projected starter for the Dominican Republic, was a former teammate of Judge’s for several years on the Yankees. Catcher Austin Wells, who was born in Arizona but is of Dominican descent, is one of Judge’s current teammates. And, of course, there’s Juan Soto, who teamed up with Judge to lead the Yankees to an American League pennant in 2024 before famously defecting to the crosstown rival Mets in free agency the following offseason. ICYMI: Dominican Republic run-rules Korea Getty ImagesKorea’s pitching staff, led by 39-year-old former MLB All-Star Hyun-Jin Ryu, was not match for the juggernaut Dominican Republic lineup earlier Friday. The D.R. scored 10 runs for the fourth time in five games this WBC tournament, chasing Ryu in the second, tacking on another handful in the third, then triggering the run rule thanks to a “walk-off” home run from Yankees catcher Austin Wells on the seventh to win 10-0. The Dominican Republic has now scored 49 runs in five games, coming out to an absurd average of 9.8 runs per game. Katie Woo recaps all the action from another display of Dominican domination in Miami.All the pressure’s on Skenes As Johnny touched on below, the Dominican Republic has absolutely demolished everyone in its path, with its lineup full of MLB superstars hitting like it. Just look at the names: Fernando Tatis Jr. Juan Soto. Julio Rodríguez. Manny Machado. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. WHEW. Budding Pirates superstar O’Neil Cruz can’t even get regular playing time because this lineup is so loaded — oh, and did I mention that some guy named Albert Pujols is the team’s manager for this tournament, with Nelson Cruz as the general manager? And retired icons like David Ortiz, Pedro Martinez, Adrian Beltre and even 88-year-old Juan Marichal have been hanging around the clubhouse, dispensing wisdom on the current generation.The good news for Team USA — and its lineup full of slumping stars — is that it sends its best pitcher to the mound on Sunday in Paul Skenes. His task? Tame this “Plátano Power” lineup that nobody has been able to stop thus far. The 23-year-old Skenes, fresh off his first of likely many Cy Young-winning seasons, is one of the only pitchers on the planet who seems like he could be up to the task, coming off a dominant start against Mexico on Monday.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementYour views: Credit for Canada’s run Getty ImagesHere’s what you had for us in the discussion page as Team USA saw off Canada, eventually. Plenty of love for the Canadian effort … 💬 Tim S: “Great game. Can’t believe we left two guys on in the 7th. That was the difference.”💬 Bosh S: “The Toro error was painful. It was going to take a great throw to get Bregman, but cost them two runs … Great effort, Canada. First time in the quarterfinals after beating PR and Cuba, and showed up well against a juggernaut. Proud of the players and the program.”💬 Brennan L: “Solid effort by Canada. Definitely overmatched and they fought back and had a chance. Can’t be mad at that.”💬 John S: “They did OK. If that’s the USA top game then they’ll have a hard time getting to the finals.”The U.S. will get to prove how much else it has in the locker come the semifinals. Remember, you can join the discussion right here and you can always send your thoughts to us in an email too: live@theathletic.comUSA vs. Dominican Republic: Two star-powered teams with very different pathsThe dust has settled, and two teams that were on a collision course for a matchup at some point in the World Baseball Classic will meet in the semifinals. Team USA and Team Dominican Republic, federations heavy on All-Stars, MVPs, Silver Sluggers, Gold Glovers and Cy Young Award winners, will meet Sunday at loanDepot park for a spot in the WBC championship.To get there, the D.R. has done nothing but crush the opposition, tying the record for the most home runs in a tournament (14) on a walk-off that mercy-ruled Korea out of the quarterfinals, 10-0. The U.S. needed help from Italy, then a strong performance from Logan Webb against Canada.This will be the first U.S.-vs.-Dominican Republic matchup since the 2017 WBC. There, the sides split the series 1-1, though Team USA ultimately got the last laugh, besting the Dominicans in the quarterfinals en route to winning its first WBC championship.It’s a coin flip between who will win, but I’ve outlined three things in the article below that will ultimately define the matchup.PCA anticipating clash with D.R.Pete Crow-Armstrong also got to speak about the prospect of facing Dominican Republic in Miami. It’s going to be some ball game …💬 “I expect to be the away team for sure, but that’s what we’re looking forward to. We want the electricity, the energy in the crowd. That’s why we’re throwing Mr. (Paul) Skenes out there, for whatever he’s gonna give them.“It’s gonna be good.”Yes it is and The Athletic will be right there, ready and waiting for the action. PCA: ‘Time to wake up’ Getty ImagesPete Crow-Armstrong has truly made his mark on the U.S. team through the World Baseball Classic. He is also aware of how it’s looked too.You get the sense the U.S. will look for better when it switches Houston for Miami. Here’s what he said on the broadcast to Ken Rosenthal … 💬 “Yeah, I don’t think this entire time in Houston has been all that pretty but we know what we have in this clubhouse, and we got guys like (Bednar) that are gonna go shut innings down like they did tonight.“It’s just most important that when it’s not always the easiest or the cleanest, we’re still getting the job done some way, somehow.“So we’re looking to really wake up one of these days now.”USA-Dominican Republic WBC historyThe last time Team USA faced the Dominican Republic in the World Baseball Classic, it brought about one of the most iconic moments in WBC history.With the U.S. clinging to a 4-2 lead in the seventh inning of the 2017 WBC quarterfinals in San Diego, D.R. slugger Manny Machado — the captain of the 2026 Dominican team — launched a ball that was sailing over the right-center field fence at Petco Park ... Until his then-Baltimore Orioles teammate Adam Jones brought it back!The U.S. would go on to win the WBC for the first (and only) time in tournament history while the Dominican Republic had yet to make it back to this point in the tournament... until now.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementOne relieved reliever Getty ImagesDavid Bednar found a way. What he did in the seventh inning to get out of a two-on, no-out jam, was a clutch moment — and he knew it.Here’s the reliever’s thoughts, speaking to Ken Rosenthal on the broadcast: 💬 “Just find a way. Just bear down and get it done … You’re just trusting what Cal (Raleigh) was putting down and the crowd really got into it towards the end. It was absolutely electric. “Those were big outs. I got myself in a little bit of a jam and it was just finding a way out of it.”Webb was wonderful Imagn ImagesNot much more could have been asked of Logan Webb tonight. The Giants ace shut down Canada and gave Team USA time to build a lead, a luxury it did not have in the loss against Italy earlier this week. Webb used his allotted 71 pitches to scatter four hits across 4.2 shutout innings, racking up five strikeouts and only allowing one walk in the process. His first WBC is over, and it was a sensational one.…but biggest bats still cold Getty ImagesBryce Harper is struggling through an atrocious WBC, going 0-for-5 with two strikeouts tonight. Bobby Witt Jr. went hitless as well. Aaron Judge didn’t have a hit after the first inning. The hits and RBIs that Kyle Schwarber and Alex Bregman did have didn’t even leave the infield.Team USA still won anyway because Logan Webb dominated and the bottom of its lineup is still loaded with talent. But the thumpers, the headliners or this Team USA squad, have to be better on Sunday against a Dominican Republic team whose own superstar bats have had no trouble heating up in Miami.USA’s bullpen holds firm Getty ImagesI wrote in our staff predictions poll at The Athletic before the World Baseball Classic that I thought Team USA would win not because of its offense or starting pitching, but because of its electric back end of the bullpen.While the Americans’ loaded lineup has been more sluggish than I or anyone could have anticipated, and I have no confidence in picking them against an All-Star Dominican Republic lineup that’s actually hitting like All-Stars, the U.S. bullpen showed why I thought they were being overlooked. David Bednar pulled off a high-wire tightrope act by getting out of the jam with runners on second and third, nobody out and the heart of Canada’s lineup facing him. Garrett Whitlock breezed through the eighth inning. And while Canada battled against Mason Miller, the electric Padres closer still struck out the side and showcased what makes him so good with a superb ninth inning.Now, the question facing Mark DeRosa is, how many of those guys can he turn to on Sunday night after Paul Skenes against the most talented — and hottest — lineup in the WBC field?Canada will rue missed chances Imagn ImagesIn this tournament and in this game, Team Canada showed it belonged. The Canadians got a big swing from Bo Naylor and a bunch of good innings from young relievers. This game came down to their thwarted seventh-inning rally. Josh Naylor had a full count and two runners in scoring position with no outs; he popped out. Then Tyler O’Neill struck out, and so did Owen Caissie. They had a chance — a real chance — and fell just short.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementU.S. gets ugly win but sets date with D.R.Team USA is moving on to the WBC semis after downing Canada, 5-3, in Houston. It wasn’t an effortless win against Canada whatsoever. Canada had the tying run on second base with no outs in the seventh inning. But they got the job done.It’s likely to be Paul Skenes against Luis Severino in the anticipated U.S.-D.R. clash in the semis. The D.R. lineup has been on fire in a way the Americans haven’t in recent games. Perhaps Skenes can be the stopper.Team USA beats Canada, punches ticket to WBC semifinal clash with Dominican Republic HOUSTON — The United States needed help to move on to the quarterfinals of the World Baseball Classic. When they got there on Friday, the Americans reasserted themselves behind Logan Webb with a 5-3 victory over Canada before 38,054 at Daikin Park. The win sets up a star-studded semifinal against the Dominican Republic on Sunday in Miami. The Dominicans thumped Korea, 10-0, to remain undefeated in the tournament, having outscored opponents by 41 runs in their five victories. The United States was coming off a surprising loss to Italy, whose subsequent victory over Mexico allowed the Americans to advance. Now they are poised to use their best starter, Paul Skenes, against the fearsome Dominican lineup.USA gets it done!▶️ Mason Miller strikes out the side, and Team USA is on to the WBC semifinals against the Domonican Republic! | Final - USA 5, Canada 3Miller too good Imagn ImagesCanada is making Mason Miller work, but his stuff is just overpowering.
